measurement: v2-i G-TRIVIAL — the naive prior, tested against a chooser that can now SEE
HOW_TO_READ_THIS: n = 11 distinct problems. The headline is problems solved.
the_result: under the inspect-first loop the naive prior LOSES two problems — 4 of 11 down to 2 — while RAISING localisation from 38.8% to 41.2% and raising cost from 8.82 to 10.14 actions. Better aim, worse outcome, more spend.
why_this_is_the_sharpest_version_of_the_: on the BLIND loop, forcing the symptom region was worth about +1 episode: the agent was guessing, so overriding its guess cost little. On the OBSERVING loop the same rule costs two problems, because it now overrides a choice made WITH evidence. THE DAMAGE A NAIVE PRIOR DOES SCALES WITH HOW GOOD THE CHOOSER UNDERNEATH IT IS — and that is measured here rather than argued, by running the identical rule against the same task set under two loops.
and_localisation_is_now_DEFINITIVELY_the: 41.2% localisation with 2 problems solved, against 38.8% localisation with 4. The arm that aims better solves less. Any bar written on localisation accuracy would have passed this arm.

A_CORRECTION_TO_MY_OWN_DETERMINISM_CLAIM.observed: 2 of 11 signatures produced MORE THAN ONE outcome in this arm (v2-i baseline had 0).
A_CORRECTION_TO_MY_OWN_DETERMINISM_CLAIM.cause: the harness raises decoding temperature after consecutive wasted steps (EXPLORE_TEMP). An arm that wastes more steps therefore breaks the identical-task-identical-outcome property that makes n exactly 11.
A_CORRECTION_TO_MY_OWN_DETERMINISM_CLAIM.what_it_changes: n = 11 is exact for arms that stay greedy and is a near-bound for arms that explore. It does not rescue the episode counts — 2 signatures splitting does not turn 80 episodes into 80 observations — but 'identical outcome, always' was too strong as I first wrote it, and the qualifier belongs in the paper.

bounds: G-trivial is handed task['bug_class'], the TRUE class, so this is an ORACLE on region AND class losing to an agent that simply looked first.
Not a controlled comparison of the rule alone: the forced hypothesis changes every subsequent prompt.
